NYC inspection records, 2010 to 2026

Ghost Storefronts

New York City's list of open businesses is only as current as the last inspection. This is how stale it gets, how to tell before a visit, and how many closed businesses are probably still on the books.

1,182,668 storefront inspection records · Snapshot August 2026

17.4%of 2025 inspection visits found the business already closed48%of those businesses were last seen open 3 or more years earlier1 in 4RadioShack and Payless stores never got a closure record after the chains shut down5,722businesses still listed as open would likely be found closed if visited today

05 · Can it be predicted?

A one-line rule does most of the work

Ranking visits by months since the business was last seen open puts a closed business in 55% of the top 10%. The best model using the same history adds 2.9 points on 2025 data and 8.9 on 2019 data.

Its probabilities can be read as rates

When the LightGBM model says about 59%, 58% of those visits find the business closed.

View data
TestRankerTop-10% precisionvs one-line rule
Old system, tested on 2019LightGBM53.8%-0.7 pts (95% CI -2.1 to +0.9)
Old system, tested on 2019Logistic regression63.4%+8.9 pts (95% CI +7.9 to +9.8)
Old system, tested on 2019One-line rule54.6%baseline
Live system, tested on 2025LightGBM57.6%+2.9 pts (95% CI +2.0 to +3.7)
Live system, tested on 2025LightGBM + program59.2%+4.5 pts (95% CI +3.5 to +5.1)
Live system, tested on 2025Logistic regression57.0%+2.3 pts (95% CI +1.5 to +3.1)
Live system, tested on 2025One-line rule54.7%baseline

Models train on earlier years and are tested on a later year they never saw. Lines are 95% intervals from resampling businesses. "+ program" assumes the inspection program is known before the visit.

06 · How many ghosts

An estimated 5,722 businesses listed as open would be found closed today

That is 13% of the 43,447 businesses seen open since 2023 (95% interval 5,443 to 5,986). Older records are left out: the model gives them about a coin flip because it never learned from businesses that stale.

Counted: seen open since 2023Left out: older than anything the model learned from

09 · Method and limits

How this was built

A Python and MongoDB pipeline over 1,182,668 storefront inspection records, 2010 to 2026. Every number on this page is generated from the pipeline's outputs.

  1. NYC Open DataInspection archive 2010 to 2023, live system 2023 to 2026, plus MongoDB's 2015 sample
  2. RawPaged API pulls loaded into MongoDB unchanged
  3. SilverOne schema across both systems; outcome and industry crosswalks
  4. Geo + identity2dsphere $geoWithin to neighborhoods; businesses linked across the 2023 switch
  5. GoldOne row per visit with features from earlier visits only ($setWindowFields, $merge)
  6. ModelsRule, logistic regression, LightGBM; Platt calibration; clustered bootstrap
  7. OutputsNotebooks, CSV exports, this page

What this does not claim

  • A closure record needs a visit. Rates reflect where and why inspectors went.
  • A business is a linked identity in the record. Name and unit changes can split one shop into two.
  • The estimate means recorded closed if visited, from a model trained on visits the city chose to make.
  • Tried and dropped because the data could not support them: storefront turnover, reopenings after padlocks, vacancy, and wasted trips.

Data: NYC Department of Consumer and Worker Protection inspections, via NYC Open Data. Built with Python, MongoDB, scikit-learn, LightGBM and Vega-Lite. Source.
